name: 2019 livery
description: A light gray fuselage with a huge tone-on-tone SAS logo across the forward cabin; the blue fin flows down over the rear fuselage to the belly ahead of the tailplane, with the white SAS logo low on the fin. Blue sharklets, gray engines with a blue ring behind the inlet and 'Scandinavian' on the cowling; small Danish, Norwegian and Swedish flags aft and under the cockpit.

sources.title: SAS press release on the 2019 livery
sources.note: The livery's introduction in 2019 (A350 and A320neo).

sources.title: Airbus A320-251N (c-n 10265, SE-RUF) 2025-09-24 (CC BY-SA 4.0)
sources.note: Right side in flight, 2025-09-24: the gray body, big SAS, blue wrap, engine ring and 'Scandinavian', SkyTeam logo, flags. Re-checked 2026-11-15: fitted (flipped) to the measured A320 shape, doors pinned: the blue wrap's edge agrees; the fin's SAS measured on it.

logoGray.name: tone-on-tone gray of the big SAS

areas.name: blue wrap from the fin down over the rear fuselage

logos.description: The Danish, Norwegian and Swedish flags side by side, small, above the windows ahead of the blue wrap.
The three flags again, tiny, under the cockpit windows above the aircraft's Viking name.
The SkyTeam swirl logo with 'SKYTEAM' below, small, between the cockpit windows and the forward door (since SAS joined SkyTeam in September 2024).

titles.style: The SAS logo enormous across the forward cabin, from above the windows to below them, a shade lighter and more silvery than the fuselage: heavy italic rounded capitals.
The SAS logo in white across the lower fin, reading normally on both sides: heavy italic rounded capitals.
Dark gray upright humanist sans, mixed case, along the cowling behind the blue ring.

notes: Drawn from right-side photos of A320neos; the design is symmetrical so the left is assumed to match (the SAS logos read normally on both sides). The belly under the blue wrap and the underside are not seen in these photos. Each aircraft carries its Viking name under the cockpit (varies, not drawn). The tail cone's last few percent look gray, left in the base color. A350s and A321LRs wear the same scheme. Aircraft delivered before late 2019 still wear the 1998 scheme (gray body, 'Scandinavian' and 'Airlines' titles round the forward windows, blue on the fin only, red engines): drawn as standard-1998 (2026-11-21), with SE-ROG tagged in airframes/SAS.json. Checked 2026-11-21 against SE-RUF (2025) and SE-ROZ (2022) again: they wear this scheme as drawn. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on SE-RUF fitted to the A320 shape: the fin's 'SAS' is smaller and longer than drawn (baseline y 0.12, cap 0.17 of the span, x 0.14-0.89); the wrap's edge, already right, drawn as a curve.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation (2026-11). The 2019 scheme replaced the 1998 livery with 'Scandinavian' titles (standard-1998), not yet on every aircraft.
